concept.name: FX future
concept.definition: A standardized, centrally cleared futures contract on the exchange rate between two currencies, traded on a regulated FX marketplace. It fixes today the rate at which one currency will be exchanged for another on a specified future settlement date, offering a cleared, transparent alternative to over-the-counter forwards.
concept.intuition: An FX future is a currency forward repackaged as an exchange product: standard sizes, standard dates, a clearinghouse guarantee, and a public price.
concept.mechanics: Contracts have fixed sizes and standardized quarterly settlement dates; they are margined and marked to market daily and are mostly offset or cash-settled rather than delivered. Because the clearinghouse interposes itself between buyer and seller, counterparty risk is mutualized, unlike bilateral forwards.
concept.failure_modes: Fixed contract sizes and dates can mismatch the exact exposure being hedged, leaving basis risk. Daily marking produces margin calls on adverse moves, and the futures-forward basis means the locked rate differs slightly from OTC forward rates.
concept.misconceptions: That FX futures and FX forwards are the same instrument — forwards are bilateral, customizable, and settle once at maturity, while futures are standardized, cleared, and settled daily. Also, retail spot forex is not the futures market: it is a separate, dealer-intermediated market.
concept.example: A U.S. importer owing 375,000 euros in three months buys three CME EUR/USD futures (125,000 euros each), fixing the dollar cost of the payment regardless of where the spot rate moves.
